findings.thunk_frequency_bound: The entry mechanism fires exactly once, so it imposes no rate bound. Re-invocation is bounded only by the dispatcher body itself: the backward span with head 0x2ae1974 and back-edge jne at 0x2ae21ff (taken while the body 0x5cdf300 called at 0x2ae21f7 returns non-null) encloses both driver call sites (driver_a 0x2ae1a47, driver_c 0x2ae1eeb), so per dispatcher-loop iteration each driver runs once and, per #2741, each gate is called twice by its driver.
findings.thunk_mechanism: SETTLED. _start (0x1419300) passes main 0x2cef8f0 to __libc_start_main (GOT 0x64df458). The main shim (0x2cef8f0..0x2cef917, exported) builds a stack closure whose first word is the thunk: lea 0x2cd8370 at 0x2cef8f7, store (%rsp) at 0x2cef8fe; it then calls the runtime entry body 0x5c99970 via GOT slot 0x64e6c30 (RELATIVE -> 0x5c99970) with rdi=&closure, rsi=static table 0x6440b48, rdx=argc, rcx=argv, r8=0. After runtime initialisation the entry body loads the table pointer it saved and calls the function pointer at [table+0x28] at 0x5c99e21; that slot (0x6440b70, RELATIVE) holds trampoline 0x292c5c0 (exported), which loads closure[0] into rdi (0x292c5c1) and calls the 5-byte indirect caller 0x2c7bb70 (exported), whose `call *%rdi` at 0x2c7bb71 invokes the thunk. So the thunk is invoked once per process, on the main thread, by program entry -- not via a registered table slot in a data segment, and not via runtime start-up registration: all 168 .init_array entries and the single .fini_array entry resolve elsewhere, and no direct branch, RELATIVE addend/offset, absolute qword/u32 or aligned interior word anywhere in the artifact names the thunk or the dispatcher. (The runtime entry body is the one body in the chain a relocation does name: GOT slot 0x64e6c30, the very slot the shim calls through.)
findings.window_a_2b90b05: The call at 0x2b90b05 uses instance rbx+0xf0 (lea at 0x2b90af3); the checker entry byte is [rbx+0x180] (instance+0x90), tested ==3 right after the call at 0x2b90b12. The setup block 0x2b90af3 has exactly two inbound edges in the whole .text: jmp at 0x2b90de2, immediately after the zero store movb $0,[rbx+0x180] at 0x2b90ddb; and jmp at 0x2b9087e, which is case 4 of jump table 0x607328 (dispatched on byte [rbx+0xca], loaded at 0x2b90725, indirect jump at 0x2b9074d) with no store to the entry byte on its path. The only store to [rbx+0x180] in the whole body is the zero store at 0x2b90ddb (store census). On the table edge the checker therefore receives the byte as last written -- by checker_a itself (3 on its predicate-nonzero arm) or by code outside this body -- and the zero-before-call invariant of #2741 does NOT hold for this window.
findings.window_b_2cc7fb5: The call at 0x2cc7fb5 uses instance r15+0x240 (lea at 0x2cc7fa6); the checker entry byte is [r15+0x2d0] (instance+0x90), tested ==3 right after the call at 0x2cc7fc6. The setup block 0x2cc7fa6 has exactly two inbound edges in the whole .text: jmp at 0x2cc92c6, immediately after the zero store movb $0,[r15+0x2d0] at 0x2cc92be; and case 4 of jump table 0x60bdb8 (dispatched on byte [r15+0x1da], loaded at 0x2cc21d0, indirect jump at 0x2cc21f2) with no zeroing store on its path. The entry byte has exactly two stores in the body (store census): the zero store at 0x2cc92be and, at 0x2cc5125, a non-constant store mov %cl,[r15+0x2d0] in a record-duplication phase, where cl is the byte copied from [r15+0x10d] (loaded at 0x2cc5031). The zero-before-call invariant of #2741 does NOT hold for this window either.

open_edges: Whether the un-zeroed table edges (0x607328 case 4, 0x60bdb8 case 4) are exercised with a nonzero entry byte at runtime is a dynamic question: statically the byte can be 3 (left by a previous checker_a call) or a copied value (window B), but which object states actually reach those cases is not decidable from these two bodies alone.
The two checker_a clone callers of the gate_a mirror family (census in #2741 records.json, checker_a_clone sites) were not re-traced here; their zero-before-call status stays as #2741 left it.

The dispatcher loop tail callee 0x5cdf300 is identified only as the body whose non-null return keeps the loop running (it sits in the TLS accessor cluster next to the destructor 0x5cdf410 of #2741); its own body is not traced in this packet.
